newsitem.title: CANADA: Two-thirds of CWB barley ballots mailed back - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: Two-thirds of CWB barley ballots mailed back - KPMG.

text.p: Two-thirds of mail-in ballots on whether the Canadian Wheat Board should retain its monopoly on feed and malt barley exports were returned by the eve of the close of the vote, consultant firm KPMG said.
"At this point, we've got just over 50,000 ballots. They've been coming in at a rate of about 1,000 a day or so and the response is fairly high already," KPMG associate Joanne Pindera told Reuters.
About 76,000 Prairie farmers were asked whether they want to retain the status quo or export barley via private firms.
The voter response rate reached 65.8 percent Wednesday.
Ballots post-marked after February 28 will not be enumerated, Pindera said.
About 30 percent of barley grown on the Prairies is exported and the balance is fed to livestock or brewed in Canada.
Western Canada produced about 15 million tonnes of barley in 1996, private and Statistics Canada estimates show.
